Cue 01 · Act I · The problem Illustrative programme

You went to the event.You saw 7 sessions.23 went on without you.

7 seen23 missed · 77% of the programme

Two days, three stages, thirty sessions. Parallel programming means even the most diligent attendee sees a quarter of it. The rest walks out the door, and so does most of what sponsors paid to put on stage.

Aftershow™ is built for the 75% nobody saw.

Cue 03 · Act II · The engine Real · Tape One

Three lenses before a single cut.

A sizzle reel picks moments by feel. Aftershow builds a brief first, then judges every line of the talk against all three lenses. A line that serves only one of them doesn't make the cut.

1

The talk

"Is This Really Creativity?" Are we measuring creativity by how hard a thing was to make, or by the value it holds, however it was made?

2

The event

Campaign360's 2026 theme was "Human Connection and Intelligent Marketing." One headline topic was using AI without sacrificing originality.

3

The industry, now

Cannes Lions 2026 added an AI Craft category. Juries stopped asking whether AI was used and started asking whether it changed the outcome. The industry is rewriting how it judges AI-made work.

The brief: find where this talk answers the question the industry is arguing about right now.

Cue 05 · Act II · The engine Real · Tape One

The engine reads the talk like an editor.

It finds the argument first, then assigns each moment a job in the story: hook, reframe, thesis, turn, close. Highlighted lines made the cut. The struck-through lines were cut by the third lens, because "even this week" was timely in May and dated by October.

0:00 / 18:54

Throughline: we confused creativity with the difficulty of execution. When execution is abundant, value moves to judgment and meaning.

Cue 07 · Act III · The world Proposed model

The footage travels. The crew doesn't.

Aftershow never sends anyone to the event. The event films the way it already does and uploads once. The packages come back to wherever the organizer, the attendees and the sponsors happen to be, whether that's Toronto, New York, Cannes or Singapore. It's one engine, held to one standard, and it delivers the morning after.

Footage up, packages backCities shown are examples, not live deployments.

Cue 08 · Act III · The world Proposed model

One page decides the quality.

The biggest variable isn't the engine. It's the input. So Aftershow publishes a Capture Standard that any AV team can meet with equipment it already owns. We don't ask an event to change how it films. We ask it to keep the audio clean and the paperwork done.

The Capture Standard · v1
AudioA clean feed from the sound desk. The transcript is the raw material, so audio matters more than picture. A bad room mic ruins a great camera.
PictureA speaker shot plus a wide. 1080p is plenty. The vertical crops are built from the speaker shot.
SlidesThe deck behind every talk. It anchors names and terms in the captions and settles the words the audio leaves uncertain.
ProgrammeThe run of show, speakers and sponsors. This becomes the event lens, the second of the three.
ReleasesSpeaker consent, collected at registration. It's handled before anyone touches a file, not chased afterward.
How it arrives
UploadDrag and drop into the event's Aftershow portal.
BucketA shared cloud folder the AV team already uses.
LinkA Vimeo or YouTube link, private or unlisted.
StreamThe livestream feed, for same-night turnaround.

Tape One met this standard with one camera and house audio.

Cue 09 · Act III · The world Proposed model

Software with an editorial spine.

The machine does the volume. A human desk signs off every selection before it ships. Over time, the desk's judgment is codified into the engine, and the margin improves with it. This is the throughline of Tape One applied to the business itself: when execution is abundant, judgment is the product.

Cue 10 · Act III · The world Proposed model

Trust is part of the product.

Conservative organizers say yes when they keep control. Every piece is approved before it publishes, every speaker has consented before filming, and every region's rules are met where the data lives.

1

Consent

Speaker releases are part of registration. Attendees opt in to their personal catch-up. Nobody is clipped by surprise.

2

Approval

The organizer sees everything before it goes out, with one click to approve and one to pull. Publishing goes to their own channel, never ours, and only on their click.

3

Compliance

GDPR in Europe, PDPA in Singapore, and regional data residency where a client requires it. The standard travels, and so does the paperwork.

The data clause: the event owns its footage and its outputs. Aftershow holds aggregated, anonymized rights across events. That one clause is what makes Act V possible.

Cue 11 · Act III · The world Proposed model

Three ways to buy it. One engine underneath.

The same pipeline is sold three ways, to three kinds of buyer. Each one feeds the same record.

Per event

The package

For one-off conferences, summits and launches. One price per event, scaled by the number of sessions. The fastest yes.

Series licence

The standard

For associations and recurring events with chapters in many cities. An annual licence puts every chapter on the same standard, so it's repeatable revenue.

White label

The partner

For AV and production houses. They film, and Aftershow powers the package under their name. They become a distribution channel, not a competitor.

Add-on · any tier

Distribution

Approve & publish, or approve & schedule, straight to the organizer's own channels. The quarter's slate goes out on a cadence, and the viewing data comes back into the sponsor report. Production gets the content made. Distribution gets it seen.

The order we go in
Beachhead

Association networks. Many small events, a forgiving production bar and a repeatable licence. This is the proof a software story needs.

Pilot

Regional festivals. Mid-size and multi-day, the place to prove same-night delivery and sponsor reporting at scale.

Flagship

Global festivals. The trophy. We arrive with proof, not a pitch.

The engine proves it works.The world proves it scales.

Thirty records, read together.
